# Security Impact Report

## PR Details

| | |
|---|---|
| PR title | Merge dev into main |
| Branch | dev |
| Report completion date | 2026-06-30 |
| Source version | backend 2026.6.12, frontend 2026.6.21-dev |
| Report file name | `2026-06-30-dev-backend-2026.6.12_frontend-2026.6.21-dev.md` |

## Summary
This PR promotes the broad `dev` branch into `main`. The diff is a full-stack release that changes backend API routes, account and 2FA flows, token storage, plugin installation and loading, update handling, system controls, diagnostics, notifications, Docker setup, GitHub workflows, frontend settings, player behavior, localization, and project documentation.

Because the branch changes 171 files and includes authentication, permissions, plugin loading, updater logic, config writes, database schema initialization, Docker access, external downloads, and frontend token handling, it is security-sensitive.

## Scope Reviewed

- Branch comparison: `main...dev` showed 171 changed files with 24,618 insertions and 2,012 deletions.
- Security report instructions and template: `.github/security-reports/README.md`, `.github/security-reports/REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`.
- Backend routing and auth surfaces: `backend/api/router.py`, `backend/api/helpers/server.py`, `backend/api/helpers/admin.py`, `backend/api/modules/account.py`, `backend/api/modules/server.py`, `backend/api/modules/setup.py`, `backend/api/modules/system.py`, `backend/api/modules/update.py`, `backend/api/modules/logs.py`, `backend/api/modules/notifications.py`, `backend/api/modules/player.py`, `backend/api/modules/server_info.py`, `backend/api/modules/plugins.py`.
- Account, password, token, 2FA, and data helpers: `backend/api/helpers/account.py`, `backend/api/helpers/passwords.py`, `backend/api/helpers/db.py`, `backend/api/helpers/notifications.py`, `backend/api/helpers/log.py`.
- Plugin and dependency execution paths: `backend/api/helpers/plugins.py`, `backend/api/helpers/plugin_installer.py`, `backend/api/helpers/plugin_functions.py`, `backend/api/helpers/plugin_db.py`, `backend/api/helpers/plugin_config.py`, built-in plugin route registration under `backend/plugins/*`.
- Update and system control paths: `backend/api/helpers/updater.py`, `backend/api/helpers/config.py`, `backend/api/helpers/config_watcher.py`, `backend/api/helpers/diagnostics.py`, `backend/api/helpers/health.py`, `backend/api/helpers/https_proxy.py`.

## Trust Boundaries
The PR changes multiple trust boundaries:

- Browser to backend: frontend requests attach the bearer access token and account token headers through `frontend/src/modules/api.ts`.
- Server-level auth to account-level auth: backend server tokens and per-account tokens are checked separately through `verify_auth`, `match_account`, and `verify_admin`.
- Admin to system: admin-only routes can read and write config, view logs, install plugins, open a terminal websocket, restart or stop services, enable safe mode, and apply updates.
- Backend to plugin code: installed plugins are imported and executed dynamically from configured plugin folders, can expose backend routes, can expose callable functions, and can request database access through `PluginDB`.
- Backend to external registries and GitHub: plugin installation downloads registry packages, update checks fetch GitHub config/version data, update application downloads GitHub tarballs, and tunnel plugins can download or invoke external tunnel binaries.
- Backend container to host Docker: Docker CLI and `/var/run/docker.sock` are available to the backend container in the reviewed compose and Dockerfile changes.
- Database to app/plugin code: schema initialization adds tokens, account metadata, notifications, update cache, and backup code tables, while plugin DB helpers add grants and table protection.
- Setup wizard to backend: setup endpoints can create and modify accounts before setup completion, while server password setup remains unauthenticated by design until a password exists.

## Authentication and Permissions
The reviewed code shows these protections:

- Server access tokens are generated with `secrets.token_hex(32)`, stored with expiration, and checked through `verify_auth`.
- Server and account passwords are hashed with bcrypt through `backend/api/helpers/passwords.py`.
- Account tokens are generated with `secrets.token_hex(32)` and checked separately from server bearer tokens.
- Account profile and token endpoints generally require both server auth and an `X-Account-Token` match through `match_account`.
- Admin-only behavior is centralized through `verify_admin`, which resolves the account token and checks the account role.
- Role changes require admin access and block self role changes.
- Password changes revoke active account tokens for the account.
- 2FA setup requires an account password, TOTP verification uses `pyotp`, and backup codes are single-use deletes.
- Admin-only routes guard log reads, plugin installation, update check/apply, system status and power controls, terminal websocket access, safe mode, and config writes.

Reviewer attention is still needed for unauthenticated or lightly scoped setup/discovery surfaces:

- `backend/api/modules/server.py` intentionally allows first-time server password setup and token issuance behavior before a password exists.
- `backend/api/modules/setup.py` exposes setup state and account creation while setup is incomplete.
- `backend/api/modules/server_info.py` exposes server/plugin metadata and plugin-file reads without bearer auth, with path traversal checks on plugin files.
- Plugin OAuth callback routes under built-in plugins are externally reachable by design and need callback-state review.

## User Data and Privacy
The PR adds or changes storage and display of user data:

- The database schema includes account names, nicknames, profile text, avatars, roles, password hashes, 2FA secrets, account tokens, server access tokens, refresh tokens, user agent/IP metadata, notifications, update cache, setup state, and backup codes.
- The reviewed account helper masks account tokens before returning token lists.
- Optional account login telemetry records IP addresses and user agents based on config.
- Notifications are scoped by account id in the notification websocket and count endpoint.
- Frontend account tokens are stored in `sessionStorage` by default, with a config option to use `localStorage`.
- Server access and refresh tokens are stored in browser `localStorage`.
- Plugin file reads return base64 data for files under the resolved plugin directory after a `relative_to` traversal check.

Remaining privacy review should focus on log content, notification text, token storage choices, avatar/base64 size handling, and whether exposing user agent/IP metadata in account token tables matches the product privacy expectations.

## Dependencies, Plugins, and External Services
The branch materially changes dependency and supply-chain behavior:

- Backend dependencies add `watchdog`, `websockets`, `psutil`, `pyotp`, and `qrcode[pil]`, and retain FastAPI, bcrypt, PostgreSQL, Pillow, TOML, and multipart parsing.
- Frontend dependencies add or update React 19, React Router, i18n packages, xterm, lucide icons, JSON5, TOML, UUID, and Vite/TypeScript tooling.
- The backend Dockerfile installs Docker CLI and Compose plugin inside the backend image.
- `docker-compose.yml` mounts `/var/run/docker.sock` into the backend container and exposes backend, frontend, database, and pgAdmin services.
- Plugin installation fetches package metadata and tarballs from configured registry endpoints, extracts tarballs using `tarfile.extractall(..., filter="data")`, skips symlinks during file install, merges config files, updates plugin config, can install plugin Python dependencies with pip, and can run `npm install` in the frontend container for frontend plugin dependencies.
- Plugin loading imports `__init__.py` from configured plugin directories and executes plugin setup functions.
- `PluginDB` protects core tables and validates table/column identifiers before plugin SQL access.
- Updater logic fetches remote GitHub version/config files, downloads branch tarballs, copies backend/frontend/root files into the compose directory, preserves selected local state, installs Python requirements, clears update cache, and restarts through Docker or host reboot flows.
- GitHub workflows with `contents: write` update backend version, frontend version, and root Docker Compose based on branch changes.

## Possible Vulnerabilities

- A compromised admin account could install plugins, write config, open a terminal websocket, restart services, or apply updates.
- A malicious or compromised plugin registry package could execute backend Python code, request allowed database access, add frontend dependencies, or affect runtime behavior after installation.
- Plugin dependency installation expands supply-chain exposure through pip and npm execution.
- Docker socket access from the backend container gives admin-controlled backend code a powerful host/container control path.
- The updater downloads and applies remote GitHub tarballs without an explicit signature verification step in the reviewed code.
- Browser storage of server tokens in `localStorage` and optional account token storage in `localStorage` increases exposure to XSS.
- Setup endpoints and unauthenticated discovery endpoints could leak or mutate state if reachable after setup assumptions are broken.
- Built-in plugin OAuth callback flows and external service integrations need state, redirect, token storage, and callback abuse review.
- Config writes are admin-gated, but unsafe configuration values could still cause filesystem writes, external calls, or service behavior changes.
- Account backup codes are stored as plaintext in the reviewed schema.

## Mitigations

- Sensitive backend routes generally require bearer auth and account-token checks, with admin-only behavior centralized through `verify_admin`.
- Passwords are bcrypt-hashed.
- Server access tokens and account tokens use `secrets.token_hex(32)`.
- Password changes revoke active account tokens.
- Token lists returned to the frontend mask token values.
- Account role changes require admin access and prevent self role edits.
- 2FA requires an existing account password, uses TOTP verification, and consumes backup codes with a delete-on-use query.
- Plugin tarball extraction uses Python's `filter="data"` and install traversal skips symlinks.
- Plugin file reads resolve paths and require the target to remain under the plugin base directory.
- Plugin database access validates SQL identifiers and protects core tables from plugin reads or writes based on the table protection map.
- Config UI access and writes are admin-gated, and frontend version config is blocked from the config write endpoint.
- Update application preserves selected local state folders and files rather than replacing everything.
- GitHub Actions set explicit `contents: write` only where version or compose automation needs to push generated changes.
- The PR now includes this required security impact report for reviewer focus.

## Remaining Risks or Questions

- Confirm whether the PR should be ready for review or remain draft when opened.
- Confirm the exact local test commands or manual checks run by the PR author. The author reported local testing, added or updated tests where needed, and checked existing behavior, but this report preparation did not rerun the application test suite.
- Review whether server tokens should remain in `localStorage` or move to a stricter storage model.
- Review whether backup codes should be hashed before storage.
- Review whether setup endpoints are unreachable or harmless after setup completion in all deployment modes.
- Review whether unauthenticated `server_info` endpoints expose too much plugin or config metadata.
- Review plugin registry trust, package signature or checksum verification, dependency installation policy, and whether plugin install should require stronger confirmation.
- Review updater trust in branch tarballs and whether release artifacts should be pinned or signed.
- Review the operational risk of mounting `/var/run/docker.sock` into the backend container.
- Review whether Docker Compose dev defaults, including published PostgreSQL and pgAdmin ports and default pgAdmin credentials, are appropriate outside development.
- Review OAuth callback handling and external API token storage for Spotify, SoundCloud, tunnels, playlists, and artists plugins.
- Review log output for secrets, tokens, IP addresses, user agents, and sensitive profile data.
